40 Which statement about radioactive decay is correct?
A
Neutrinos are always emitted during -decay.
B
The -particles emitted from a radioactive sample have a continuous range of kinetic energies.
C
The – particles emitted from a radioactive sample have a continuous range of kinetic energies.
D
The proton number of a nucleus decreases by four when it undergoes -decay.

hints: Notice the contrast in the question between alpha-particles and beta-minus particles both described as having a continuous range of kinetic energies.
Recall that beta-minus decay also emits an antineutrino, so the total decay energy is shared between two light particles, while alpha-decay has only the alpha-particle and daughter nucleus.
Check the alpha-decay equation $^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow ^{A-4}_{Z-2}Y + ^{4}_{2}He$ for the change in proton number $Z$ and whether any neutrino is present.
walkthrough: Write the alpha-decay equation as $^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow ^{A-4}_{Z-2}Y + ^{4}_{2}He$. No neutrino appears, and $Z$ falls by 2 while $A$ falls by 4.
Recall the beta-minus equation as $^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow ^{A}_{Z+1}Y + ^{0}_{-1}e + \bar{\nu}_e$. An electron antineutrino is emitted with the electron.
Apply energy conservation: alpha-decay is two-body, so for a given parent to daughter transition the alpha-particle must carry a fixed discrete kinetic energy.
Apply the same idea to beta-minus decay: it is three-body, so the fixed total energy is shared randomly between the electron and the nearly undetected antineutrino.
Therefore electrons show a continuous range of kinetic energies from near zero to a maximum, while statements A, B and D contradict the equations above. This is option C.

A.explanation: Alpha-decay emits only a $^4_2He$ nucleus and the daughter nucleus. No neutrino or antineutrino is involved; they occur in beta-decay via the weak interaction.

B.explanation: Alpha-decay is a two-body break-up, so energy and momentum conservation give the alpha-particle a discrete kinetic energy, seen as line spectra, not a continuous range.

C.explanation: Beta-minus decay is a three-body decay sharing the available energy between electron, antineutrino and recoil nucleus, so the electron has a continuous spectrum up to a maximum.

D.explanation: In alpha-decay the nucleon number $A$ decreases by 4 but the proton number $Z$ decreases by 2, since $^4_2He$ carries away two protons.
